text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: DO: Replace the current prompt-review system with a shared log that records every prompt sent, its engine, routing rule, and timestamp. This makes changes auditable and lets us spot regressions or drift in real time. The trade-off is storage cost and slight latency from logging—but the clarity it gives outweighs that.

name: Gauge
text: Sprocket’s shared log buries decisions under noise—no discipline, no rollback, no way to prove a regression was a one-off. A better alternative: a minimal, versioned changelog that ties each prompt change to a decision record and a rollback point. Settle it by running a 2-week pilot: if the log doesn’t cut mean-time-to-recovery for prompt regressions, scrap it.

name: Sprocket
text:
DO: Adopt a minimal, versioned changelog for prompts and engines, storing only the delta (what changed, why, and who approved it) with a rollback tag for each version. This cuts noise while keeping every decision auditable and reversible—no more digging through logs to find what broke or when. The trade-off is extra upfront work to write concise changelog entries, but it saves weeks of debugging later.

name: Gauge
text: The versioned changelog still risks becoming a graveyard of half-remembered justifications—approvals blur, "why" fades, and rollbacks become guesswork when context is lost. A better alternative: a living decision log where each entry is a short, signed artifact (decision + trade-offs + owner + expiration date) that auto-archives stale entries. Settle it by forcing every new prompt change to include a diff against the last signed decision—if the diff isn’t justified in the log, the change is rejected.

name: Ratchet
text: DECISION: Adopt a living decision log—each entry is a signed artifact (decision + trade-offs + owner + expiration) stored in a versioned repo, replacing the shared log and versioned changelog. The result must deliver a working template and first 10 entries within 5 days, owned by Sprocket.
